subject: MAP: Data handling & compliance - FinHealth (post-call follow-up)
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@finhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: MAP: Data handling & compliance - FinHealth (post-call recap)

Hi Sara — great to meet earlier today, and thanks for walking us through FinHealth's ingestion and compliance needs. Quick recap + proposed MAP milestone for data handling and compliance so we can align next steps. Please let me know if I missed anything.

1) Milestone: Data handling & compliance requirements (retention, logging, audit trails, PHI/PII constraints)
- Target close date: 2026-11-30 (open to earlier if SOC2 evidence and questionnaire returned sooner)
- Dependencies: FinHealth security questionnaire + data flow diagram, legal review of contract redlines, SOC2 report or equivalent evidence
- Redwood responsibilities: provide SOC2 summary and control mapping, describe data retention defaults and configurable retention, outline audit logging and access controls, clarify PHI/PII handling options (hosted vs dedicated/private)
- FinHealth responsibilities: share completed security questionnaire, confirm required retention windows and any regional residency restrictions, provide list of PHI data types and ingest pipeline points
- Owners: Aditya (sales lead) — coordinate MAP and timeline; Marissa (security/solutions) — deliver SOC2 artifacts, security answers; FinHealth: Sara (security lead) — complete questionnaire + data flow diagram

2) Short answers from today (we'll formalize in the MAP doc):
- Encryption: Redwood encrypts in transit and at rest by default; for stricter key control we can support customer-managed keys on Private deployments or dedicated options — Marissa to confirm specifics.
- Logging/retention: Hosted API keeps operational logs by default with configurable retention; we can agree to retention windows in contract and limit persisted prompt storage per customer requirements.
- PHI/PII: By default we do not surface raw PHI to third parties and have controls to redact/store only what customers allow; dedicated/private deployments provide stronger isolation and audit controls.

3) Next steps:
- Attached: MAP-draft-v1.xlsx (initial milestone table), FinHealth_SOC2-summary.pdf
- Sara: please return the completed security questionnaire and a data flow diagram by 2026-10-25 if possible
- Redwood (Marissa/Aditya): update MAP with responsibilities and proposed deliverables by 2026-10-21
- Schedule a follow-up call to review the updated MAP and any legal questions — propose 10/22 or 10/23

Thanks again — I’ll follow up with an updated MAP next week.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@finhealth.com>

Date: 2026-10-19T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Data handling & compliance - FinHealth (post-call recap)

Aditya — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying questions before we complete the questionnaire:

1) Data residency: We need assurance that PHI from US customers remains in US regions only. Can Redwood guarantee regional routing for hosted API, or should we plan for Dedicated/Private?
2) PHI handling: Does Redwood ever persist full prompt/response payloads? We prefer no storage of PHI unless encrypted and explicitly permitted.
3) Keys & encryption: For hosted customers, do you offer CMEK or is that only on Private? If only Private, what are the recommended mitigations for hosted?

We attached our security questionnaire (FinHealth_Security_Questionnaire.pdf) — we still have a few internal approvals to get but wanted to surface the above. Would also appreciate a one-page summary of log retention policies (how long audit logs are stored and how to request deletion) and any SOC2 control mapping you can share.

Would it help to sign an NDA before we exchange any redlined contractual language? Happy to get that started if helpful.

Thanks,
Sara Jenkins
Security Lead | FinHealth
sara.jenkins@finhealth.com

Date: 2026-10-19T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Data handling & compliance - FinHealth (post-call recap)

Thanks for the thread, Aditya — adding internal notes and proposed responses we should send to Sara. I’ll own the SOC2 artifacts and the control mapping. Dev, can you validate the short answers on retention and PHI handling and confirm whether we can provide CMEK for a hosted tier or whether that is Private-only?

Proposed clarifications to send back to FinHealth (draft):
- Regional routing: For hosted API we route requests by region and can prefer US regions for US customers. However, for contractual guarantees of locality we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments where we can provide stronger contractual commitments and network controls.
- Prompt/response persistence: By default, Redwood keeps short-term operational logs to support debugging and abuse detection; we offer configuration to minimize or disable persistent storage of prompts for customers with strict requirements. We can include a contractual clause to prohibit retention of PHI in logs for FinHealth if required.
- Encryption/CMEK: Customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) are currently available for Private deployments and some Dedicated configurations. For hosted customers we offer strong encryption at rest but CMEK is limited — we should offer compensating controls (shorter retention, dedicated routing, additional audit logging) while the customer considers Dedicated/Private.

Next steps (internal):
- Marissa: prepare SOC2 summary + control mapping, a one-page log retention summary, and answers to the questionnaire by 2026-10-21. (Attachment: security_answered_v1.pdf)
- Dev: confirm technical feasibility of disabling prompt persistence per-customer and document steps for data flow diagram by 2026-10-21.
- Aditya: propose follow-up times and update MAP with clarified owners + target dates (see thread)

If we can get the questionnaire and data flow by 10/25 we should be able to aim for a legal review and target closing the MAP milestone by 11/15; if SOC2 evidence is delayed, keep 11/30 as fallback.

Marissa Cole

Proposed next step: 30-minute review call to walk through the MAP + questionnaire answers — would 10/22 at 10:00 AM PT or 10/23 at 2:00 PM PT work for you? We can also get the NDA queued if you'd like.
